curated.instructions: omr/instructions/42036-1-2.pdf (the street motorcycle, the book marked 1, steps 1-40); omr/instructions/42036-1-1.pdf (the book marked 2) builds the alternate model

functions.does: Pushed along, the rear wheel runs the four-cylinder engine: a 24 tooth sprocket on the rear wheel drives a chain to a 16 tooth sprocket on the swing arm's pivot axle, a row of 16 tooth gears carries the turn forward and up to a 24 tooth gear, and that drives an 8 tooth gear on the crankshaft, so the four pistons pump up and down, about four and a half times per turn of the wheel.
functions.source: book: steps 1-7 of the gear train (pages 17-19), 17-23 (rear wheel, sprockets, gears; pages 22-29), the engine's steps 1-16 (pages 31-36, the crankshaft and pistons drawn 1:1), 25 (engine fitted, page 37) and 28 (chain, page 40)
functions.note: the gear count is read from the model: 24 tooth sprocket to 16 tooth (1.5), then 24 tooth to the 8 tooth on the crankshaft (3)

functions.does: The rear wheel rides on a swing arm pivoted under the seat, with a yellow shock absorber from the frame to the swing arm, so the rear wheel moves up and down; the chain runs round the sprocket on the pivot axle, so the drive to the engine keeps working.
functions.source: book: steps 13 (shock absorber, page 11), 17-19 (swing arm and its pivot axle, pages 23-25)

functions.does: The front wheel rides between two long shock absorbers, a telescopic front fork, so it moves up and down.
functions.source: book: front wheel steps 1-9 (pages 41-45), fork steps 1-15 (pages 46-52); inferred: that it's meant to move

functions.does: The shock absorbers' springs hold the bike up and spring back.
functions.source: book: steps 13 and the fork's steps
functions.skip: springs only matter under force; the suspension moves freely without them

functions.does: The handlebars steer the front fork and wheel.
functions.source: book: handlebar steps 1-7 (pages 57-58), steps 29-31 (front end fitted, pages 53-55); inferred: that it steers, the book draws no arrow

functions.does: The kickstand under the right side swings down to hold the bike up, and folds back up.
functions.source: book: step 32 (page 56); inferred: that it folds
book: steps 20 (rear wheel) and the front wheel's step 5
